ledger.claim: The trace establishes a deviation on this trip's own evidence. Between the recorded pickup and the recorded dropoff the vehicle covered 24.6 km against a booked platform optimal of 19.6 km — an excess of 5.0 km, or 25.5% of optimal. Both limbs of the POL-RD-01 gate pass: 25.5% clears the 20% share threshold and 5.0 km clears the 0.8 km absolute floor. The deviation is therefore ESTABLISHED and the enquiry moves to exculpation and remedy.

The governing distance figure is the trace, not the rounded copy. POL-RD-01 makes gps_trace.trace_distance_km the field for the threshold test, and here it reads 24.6 km on EV-GPS-00508 — and 24.6 km is also the distance_charged_km on the fare breakdown, so the entire excess was passed through into what the rider paid. This is not a measurement artefact; it is billed distance.

The rider's initial burden under POL-RD-08 is discharged. The artifacts describe one trip — trip identifier TRP-00508 appears on the trip record, the GPS trace and the fare breakdown — and the excess above threshold is measured from a trace that is complete. The enhanced-corroboration gate in POL-RD-08 does not engage on this rider either: rider_profile.deviation_claims_60d is 0, nowhere near the four-claim trigger, so no corroboration beyond the trace is required.

There is no integrity problem for the driver to hide behind. The trace carries 205 fixes at the scheduled 10 s cadence, 100% coverage, zero gaps and a maximum gap of 0.0 s, so none of POL-RD-07 limbs (a) to (c) fires. The deviation may therefore rest on this trace alone, and no independent corroborating artifact is needed.

The external-event excuse is unavailable. The only traffic advisory artifact for this trip is MISSING: EV-ADVIS-00508-01 has no payload and carries weight 0.0 with issue code MISSING_ARTIFACT. There is thus nothing on the record that names a road or expressway segment, nothing with a validity window overlapping the time the vehicle would have reached the affected segment, and no shortest_lawful_alternative_km figure — so the capped exoneration formula in POL-RD-03 cannot be run at all. Under POL-GEN-02 a weight-0.0 artifact can carry no fact; its absence is citable and it is cited here.

ledger.claim: No rider-requested detour can be made out. The chat log for TRP-00508 contains zero messages and no waypoint_hint, so there is no rider instruction timestamped before the vehicle left the optimal corridor (or within three minutes after it), and nothing for the trace to corroborate within 200 m. POL-RD-04 cannot be run on this record and exonerates nothing.

Nor is there a relocation for the driver to re-quote against. Both pickup_amended_at and dropoff_amended_at are null on the trip record and no amended optimal distance or duration is stored, so POL-RD-05 has no field to operate on and the 19.6 km booked optimal stands as the baseline.

This is not a pooled trip, so the pooled baseline does not apply. vehicle_type on the trip record is RYDE_TAXI, not RYDE_POOL, and no solo_optimal_distance_km is carried; POL-RD-12 is inapplicable and the correct baseline is the 19.6 km booked optimal on the trip record.

With the deviation established and nothing exculpating it, the refund under POL-RD-02 is arithmetic, not discretionary. fare_breakdown.fare_model is METERED, and the multiplier is read from the fare breakdown, where surge_multiplier is 1.0. recomputed_fare = (3.80 + 0.75 × 19.6 + 0.28 × 26.0) × 1.0 + 0.80 platform fee = 26.58; charged_total is 32.57; the refund is 5.99, rounded up to SGD 6.00. That is 18.4% of the charged total, below the 90% full-refund share, so the correct outcome is PARTIAL_REFUND, not FULL_REFUND. The rider's headline figure of 32.57 is not the measure POL-RD-02 uses; the measure is charged_total less the recomputed fare.

The refund is not de minimis. The computed figure of 5.99 is well above the SGD 0.50 de_minimis_refund, so no NO_ACTION follows on that ground, and the rider must not be left carrying the charge for 5 km and the extra minutes he never needed.

The driver's 'today was peak' answer does not explain the extra distance. The only time-of-day multiplier on this fare is fare_breakdown.surge_multiplier, which reads 1.0, and surge lives nowhere else on the record; the rates actually applied are the flat card rates of SGD 0.75 per km and SGD 0.28 per minute. Time of day therefore changes nothing about the 5.0 km excess, which is a distance fact, not a pricing fact.

Nothing in the pass-through lines changes the number in either direction. There are no ERP gantry charges on this fare and no airport surcharge, so the standalone pass-through correction under POL-RD-09 is nil, and under POL-RD-09 limb (1) off-route ERP could not have been added on top of the POL-RD-02 figure in any event.

If the judge instead treats the driver's traffic assertion as a genuine invocation of the external-event excuse rather than an uncited general assertion, then that excuse is invoked with no traffic_advisory covering the CTE southbound in this window — the situation POL-RD-10 limb (5) names — and the case must escalate, which holds the disputed amount rather than collecting it from the rider. On either route through the evidence the rider does not end up paying for the unexplained 5 km.

ledger.claim: On the record's own distance figures this is a threshold-level deviation at most, not the aggravated overcharge the rider describes. The governing trace distance is 24.6 km against a 19.6 km optimal, an excess of 5.0 km or 25.51%: that clears POL-RD-01's establishment gate (more than 20% and more than 0.8 km) but falls below the materiality gate (more than 50% or more than 8.0 km), so this trip is not a 'material' deviation and the driver_profile consequences that attach only to materiality do not arise. The trace figure and the trip-record copy agree at 24.6 km, so the trace-governs rule decides nothing on this record.

The case should not be finally ruled on the present record, because the driver's external-cause defence cannot be tested either way. The driver's account is that the CTE was queued at the Braddell exit and he took the BKE-PIE instead - an excuse of the kind POL-RD-03 governs - but the traffic_advisory that clause requires is MISSING from the pool. EV-ADVIS-00508-01 carries no payload, holds weight_multiplier 0.0 and fired the issue code MISSING_ARTIFACT ('no advisory covers the CTE southbound in this window'), so the exoneration test cannot be run. Where an exculpatory clause is invoked against a cited artifact that is missing from the pool, POL-RD-10(5) makes escalation mandatory: a human reviewer decides, and the disputed amount is held rather than refunded. The absence is itself citable evidence and is not a finding for either side. I disclose that this claim rests on an artifact at weight 0.0 with issue code MISSING_ARTIFACT.

Nothing on the driver's profile aggravates the remedy. The trailing-90-day deviation flag count is 0 against 250 completed trips, so neither limb of the POL-RD-06 test is met - 0 is below the 3-flag threshold, and 0/250 is below the 0.05 ratio on a base far above 40 trips. The FULL_REFUND uplift and the driver-conduct referral that POL-RD-06 licenses where a pattern is established are therefore not earned here, and POL-GEN-01 confines this artifact to the two fields the clause names, which are the two cited.

Even on the rider's best case the arithmetic produces a narrow partial refund, not the whole SGD 32.57 contested. Recomputed against the 19.6 km optimal the fare is ((3.80 + 0.75 x 19.6 + 0.28 x 26.0) x 1.0 surge) + 0.80 platform fee = 26.58, so the refund is 32.57 - 26.58 = 5.99, rounded up to 6.00 payable - about 18.4% of charged_total, above the 0.50 de minimis but far below the 90% share that POL-RD-02 requires before FULL_REFUND displaces the partial. The rider's demand for the entire fare is not supported by the policy's own computation.

No pass-through or billing-integrity line can be added on top of that figure. The fare breakdown carries no ERP gantry lines and tolls of 0.00, so no off-route gantry correction arises under POL-RD-09(1)-(2); the airport surcharge is 0.00 on a trip that neither originates nor terminates at an airport, so POL-RD-09(4) has no phantom line to refund; and the trace passes no charged gantry. The distance-and-time recomputation is the rider's only route to any money, and it is the narrow one already computed.

The rider's wider narrative is unsupported and should not widen the remedy. 'Same route every time, never above 40' and a driver who 'took the longer way twice' cite no artifact in the bundle: the trip's chat log is empty - zero messages, both first_message_at and last_message_at null - and no pattern evidence accompanies the claim. Under POL-RD-08 assertions from either side that cite no evidence ID carry no weight, so the dispute reduces to this one completed trip's single 25.51% excess, not a course of dealing.

ruling.explanation:
To both parties: I cannot finally rule on this dispute on the present record, so the SGD 32.57 charged on the fare breakdown (EV-FARE-00508) is held — neither kept by the driver nor refunded to the rider — until a human reviewer resolves the one question the record leaves open. This is not a finding for either side (POL-RD-10). What the record shows. The trip is TRP-00508, Woodlands MRT to Novena Square on 27 Aug 2026. The platform GPS trace (EV-GPS-00508) is clean: 205 fixes at the expected 10-second cadence, 100% coverage, no gaps, longest gap 0.0 s, so POL-RD-07's impairment limbs (a) to (c) do not fire and the trace is fully usable. It measures 24.6 km against the booked optimal of 19.6 km on the trip record (EV-TRIP-00508): an excess of 5.0 km, 25.5%. That passes POL-RD-01's establishment gate (above 20% and above 0.8 km) but is below its materiality gate (above 50% or above 8.0 km), so this is not a material deviation and POL-RD-06's driver-profile check is not engaged; the driver profile (EV-DPROF-00508) shows 0 deviation flags in 90 days over 250 completed trips in any event, and the rider profile shows 0 deviation claims in 60 days, so POL-RD-08's enhancement gate does not engage either. On the clauses I can run, nothing excuses the distance: the chat log (EV-CHAT-00508) holds zero messages, so there is no POL-RD-04 rider-requested detour; no pickup or dropoff was amended and no amended optimal is stored, so POL-RD-05 has no field to operate on; the vehicle is RYDE_TAXI, not a pooled trip, so POL-RD-12 does not apply; and the fare is METERED, so POL-RD-11's upfront rules do not apply. The question I cannot answer. The driver explains the route as a response to a queue on the CTE at the Braddell exit — an external-cause defence of the kind POL-RD-03 governs. That clause can only be made out from a traffic_advisory naming a road the optimal route traverses, with a validity window overlapping the time the trace shows the vehicle would have reached the segment, matched by the actual route. The only advisory artifact for this trip, EV-ADVIS-00508-01, is MISSING from the pool: no payload, weight_multiplier 0.0, issue code MISSING_ARTIFACT, with the assessment recording that no advisory covers the CTE southbound in this window. I name the artifact, its weight and its issue code as POL-GEN-02(3) requires: at weight 0.0 it can carry no fact, and its absence is itself the citable fact. Because the artifact the clause requires is absent, the exoneration test cannot be run in either direction, and POL-RD-10(5) makes escalation mandatory where an exculpatory clause is invoked against a cited artifact that is missing from the pool — the clause's own example being 'a closure asserted with no traffic_advisory'. The driver's bare account in the counterparty statement cites no evidence ID and would in any event carry no weight under POL-RD-08; but the defence cannot be tested, and escalation under POL-RD-10 is terminal. For the reviewer, not ordered today. If the external-cause defence fails, the arithmetic under POL-RD-02 would be: recomputed fare = ((3.80 + 0.75 x 19.6 + 0.28 x 26.0) x 1.0, the surge_multiplier read from the fare breakdown) + 0.80 platform fee = 26.58, against a charged total of 32.57, giving a refund of 5.99 rounded up to SGD 6.00 — above the SGD 0.50 de minimis but far below the 90% share of charged total that would make it a full refund. That figure is not ordered now and the disputed amount stays held. What would resolve it. The LTA traffic-advisory record for the CTE southbound at the Braddell Road exit for 27 Aug 2026 between 08:20 and 08:40, or the driver's dash-cam footage for the same window. An advisory covering a closure or serious queue on the corridor the booked optimal uses would excuse the defended excess up to the POL-RD-03 cap; if there was no such event, the deviation stands and SGD 6.00 is the figure to apply. On the parties' other claims: the rider's narrative of a repeated course of dealing ('the longer way twice', 'same route every time') cites no artifact — the trip's chat log is empty — and carries no weight under POL-RD-08; the driver's 'today was peak' answer does not explain distance, since the only time-of-day multiplier on the record is fare_breakdown.surge_multiplier, which reads 1.0; and there are no ERP, toll or surcharge lines on this fare (all 0.00, on a trip that neither originates nor ends at an airport), so no standalone pass-through correction under POL-RD-09 arises in either direction and no billing-integrity referral fires. Confidence is stated below the platform's 0.70 floor because the exculpation question rests on an artifact that is not in the record.

The judge was asked 4 times on the same inputs and 3 of the 4 drafts agreed on this ruling, so it is carried, not unanimous (vote agreement 0.75).
